records.context: A workstation GPU is often shared by several jobs: a segmentation run, a measurement run and a training processing session can all hold memory on one card. Each of them sizes its batches for an empty card, so whichever allocates last runs out of memory and, before this module, stopped. This module is the one place that decides how much a spaCR GPU call may take:
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#1
records.source: A workstation GPU is often shared by several jobs: a segmentation run, a measurement run and a training run can all hold memory on one card. Each of them sizes its batches for an empty card, so whichever allocates last runs out of memory and, before this module, stopped. This module is the one place that decides how much a spaCR GPU call may take:
records.translation: En GPU i en arbetsstation delas ofta av flera jobb: en segmenteringskörning, en mätkörning och en träningskörning kan alla hålla minne på samma kort. Var och en dimensionerar sina batcher för ett tomt kort, så den som allokerar sist får slut på minne och stannade, före den här modulen. Den här modulen är det enda ställe som avgör hur mycket ett GPU-anrop i spaCR får ta:

records.context: before each batch it reads the free memory of the device and, when the batch is estimated not to fit with ``gpu_memory_margin_gb`` to spare, shrinks the batch or waits for memory to be freed;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#2
records.source: before each batch it reads the free memory of the device and, when the batch is estimated not to fit with ``gpu_memory_margin_gb`` to spare, shrinks the batch or waits for memory to be freed;
records.translation: före varje batch läser den enhetens lediga minne och, när batchen uppskattas inte få plats med ``gpu_memory_margin_gb`` till godo, krymper den batchen eller väntar på att minne frigörs;

records.context: on an out-of-memory error from PyTorch or CuPy it releases the cached blocks, halves the batch and retries the same item; after a few failed retries at batch size 1 the item executes on the CPU. No item is dropped and the processing session never stops on an out-of-memory error;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#3
records.source: on an out-of-memory error from PyTorch or CuPy it releases the cached blocks, halves the batch and retries the same item; after a few failed retries at batch size 1 the item runs on the CPU. No item is dropped and the run never stops on an out-of-memory error;
records.translation: vid ett fel om slut på minne från PyTorch eller CuPy släpper den de cachade blocken, halverar batchen och försöker samma post igen; efter några misslyckade försök vid batchstorlek 1 körs posten på CPU. Ingen post tappas och körningen stannar aldrig på grund av ett fel om slut på minne;

records.context: after each item it releases the cached memory, so a co-tenant can use it;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#4
records.source: after each item it releases the cached memory, so a co-tenant can use it;
records.translation: efter varje post släpper den det cachade minnet, så att en annan användare av kortet kan använda det;

records.context: after a run of clean items it doubles the batch again, up to the size the caller asked for;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#5
records.source: after a run of clean items it doubles the batch again, up to the size the caller asked for;
records.translation: efter en serie felfria poster fördubblar den batchen igen, upp till den storlek anroparen bad om;

records.context: ``gpu_memory_fraction`` sets a hard ceiling through ``torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction``. That call caps the memory PyTorch's caching allocator RESERVES, which is more than it has allocated by the allocator's fragmentation, so every need and cap here is sized from ``torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved`` and never below 1.5 times the allocated peak; a ceiling set lower than what the work needs is raised, with a message, rather than turning every larger item into an out-of-memory retry;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#6
records.source: ``gpu_memory_fraction`` sets a hard ceiling through ``torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction``. That call caps the memory PyTorch's caching allocator RESERVES, which is more than it has allocated by the allocator's fragmentation, so every need and cap here is sized from ``torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved`` and never below 1.5 times the allocated peak; a ceiling set lower than what the work needs is raised, with a message, rather than turning every larger item into an out-of-memory retry;
records.translation: ``gpu_memory_fraction`` sätter ett hårt tak via ``torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction``. Det anropet begränsar det minne som den cachande allokeraren i PyTorch reserverar (RESERVES), vilket på grund av allokerarens fragmentering är mer än den har allokerat, så varje behov och tak här dimensioneras utifrån ``torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved`` och aldrig under 1.5 gånger den allokerade toppen; ett tak som satts lägre än vad arbetet behöver höjs, med ett meddelande, i stället för att varje större post blir ett nytt försök efter slut på minne;

records.context: when CUDA has not been initialised yet and ``PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`` is unset, :func:`_configure` sets it to ``expandable_segments:True``, which lets the allocator grow segments in place instead of reserving new ones, so reserved memory stays close to allocated memory. An existing value is never changed, and a process that already holds a CUDA context keeps the allocator it has;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#7
records.source: when CUDA has not been initialised yet and ``PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`` is unset, :func:`_configure` sets it to ``expandable_segments:True``, which lets the allocator grow segments in place instead of reserving new ones, so reserved memory stays close to allocated memory. An existing value is never changed, and a process that already holds a CUDA context keeps the allocator it has;
records.translation: när CUDA ännu inte har initierats och ``PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`` inte är satt, sätter :func:`_configure` den till ``expandable_segments:True``, vilket låter allokeraren utöka segment på plats i stället för att reservera nya, så att reserverat minne ligger nära allokerat minne. Ett befintligt värde ändras aldrig, och en process som redan har en CUDA-kontext behåller den allokerare den har;

records.context: every process is counted with about 0.4 GB of CUDA context on top of what its allocator reserves, in the ledger and in the budget;
records.label: spacr._gpu_governor#8
records.source: every process is counted with about 0.4 GB of CUDA context on top of what its allocator reserves, in the ledger and in the budget;
records.translation: varje process räknas med ungefär 0.4 GB CUDA-kontext utöver vad dess allokerare reserverar, både i registret och i budgeten;

records.context: a ledger file under the user cache directory records what every spaCR GPU process on the machine is using and about to claim, so a new job counts what the others are about to take and an executing job shrinks while room is needed. records.context: **Layout engine** (:class:`ReportItem`, :class:`ReportBlock`, :func:`paginate`, :func:`render_report`). A report is a list of blocks, each a heading plus panel items. An item is half or full page width with a height in mm. Items are packed into rows (two half items, or one full item), rows into A4 portrait pages (210 x 297 mm). A block that does not fit the rest of a page starts on a new page; a block taller than a page flows on, row by row, with its heading repeated. Text sizes are fixed in points (never below 5 pt), so a long report gets more pages, never smaller text. Panels whose condition axis does not fit the page width are split into chunks of conditions (:func:`condition_chunks`) drawn as consecutive rows.
records.label: spacr.assay_report#2
records.source: **Layout engine** (:class:`ReportItem`, :class:`ReportBlock`, :func:`paginate`, :func:`render_report`). A report is a list of blocks, each a heading plus panel items. An item is half or full page width with a height in mm. Items are packed into rows (two half items, or one full item), rows into A4 portrait pages (210 x 297 mm). A block that does not fit the rest of a page starts on a new page; a block taller than a page flows on, row by row, with its heading repeated. Text sizes are fixed in points (never below 5 pt), so a long report gets more pages, never smaller text. Panels whose condition axis does not fit the page width are split into chunks of conditions (:func:`condition_chunks`) drawn as consecutive rows.
records.translation: **Layoutmotor** (:class:`ReportItem`, :class:`ReportBlock`, :func:`paginate`, :func:`render_report`). En rapport är en lista med block, vart och ett en rubrik plus panelposter. En post är halv eller hel sidbredd med en höjd i mm. Poster packas i rader (två halva poster eller en hel post) och rader i stående A4-sidor (210 x 297 mm). Ett block som inte får plats på resten av en sida börjar på en ny sida; ett block som är högre än en sida flyter vidare, rad för rad, med rubriken upprepad. Textstorlekar är fasta i punkter (aldrig under 5 pt), så en lång rapport får fler sidor, aldrig mindre text. Paneler vars villkorsaxel inte får plats i sidbredden delas upp i grupper av villkor (:func:`condition_chunks`) som ritas som på varandra följande rader.

records.context: **Tiles** (:func:`select_tiles`, :func:`extract_tile`, :func:`render_tile`, :func:`build_tiles`). records.context: This module is also the authority on **what an extracted-image-region PNG on disk means** -- see the "Crop PNG format" section below. In short: the current format is 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), whose red, green and blue slots hold exactly the source image data channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` names; format 1 ("legacy", unmarked) holds the same bytes for the default mapping and is returned untouched; format 2, written for eleven days in 2026, is the one that is reversed, and :func:`read_crop_png` is what reverses it back.
